title.narrative: Samoa System Transformation Grant - Agency Fees

description.narrative:
The development of Samoa’s new Education Sector Plan (ESP) 2025-2030 presents a timely opportunity to ensure full alignment between the STG strategies and the country's educational priorities. The STG programme proposal refines the priority reform outlined in the Partnership Compact while leveraging the insights from further consultations and the new ESP to design targeted interventions that respond to critical sector needs and act as catalysts for system transformation. Through this process, three strategic domains emerged as focal areas: ECE and transitions to early primary, foundational learning in primary schooling, and school-level TVET with pathways to employment and PSET. These domains were prioritised due to their potential to address systemic challenges and unlock seamless transitions that promote quality lifelong learning for all.
At the core of the programme design is a commitment to advancing teacher development, gender equality, inclusion, and community participation. These cross-cutting issues are embedded within the interventions to ensure a holistic approach to the priority reform. Specific efforts will be made to hardwire gender and equity considerations into the outcomes, ensuring inclusive and sustainable impact.
Outcome 1 focuses on enhancing ECE and transitions to primary education. While Samoa has developed several policies and tools in this area, implementation remains a significant challenge, alongside limited coordination within the subsector. These challenges create barriers to young children’s preparation for and smooth transitions into primary education. This outcome, therefore, aims to strengthen planning, coordination, and resource allocation while addressing implementation gaps in the other four core functions of ECE as identified in the ESA: curriculum development, workforce training, family and community engagement, and quality assurance.
Outcome 2 focuses on strengthening primary school aged students’ foundational literacy and numeracy skills to sustain their engagement and success at primary school and as they transition to secondary and post-secondary education and work. Where students experience literacy and numeracy success in the earlier years of compulsory schooling, they are more likely to remain engaged in secondary education and able to maximise the learning they experience within it. Utilising existing literacy and numeracy achievement datasets as diagnostic tools at the school and grade level affords primary teachers’ opportunities to design and deliver multi-tiered interventions for vulnerable student cohorts as well as provide tailored individual support for learners with additional needs. These students are otherwise at risk of progressing through their schooling without achieving the levels of literacy and numeracy skills necessary to future learning and work opportunities.
Outcome 3 targets the TVET subsector, focusing on improving pathways to PSET and employment. Secondary education faces structural bottlenecks, with high dropout rates—particularly among boys and in grades 11–12—and limited pathways for children and youth in the later years or after secondary school completion. Offering high quality, attractive and relevant TVET programmes at secondary level could facilitate the continuation of learning through higher education or provide alternate learning pathways for youth willing to enter the labour market, reducing socioeconomic and geographic inequalities and equipping young people with the skills needed to thrive. The outcome seeks to support enhanced alignment, governance and coordination within the TVET subsector and aligns with UNESCO’s global strategy for TVET support and Samoa’s vision for repackaging secondary-level TVET offerings. This outcome builds upon planned activities under MEC’s TVET repackaging exercise and includes complementary initiatives to achieve a comprehensive reform of TVET offerings within secondary education subsector.
Together, these outcomes aim to create a sustainable and inclusive education system that empowers learners at every stage, ensures equitable opportunities, and fosters lifelong learning for all in Samoa.
